sources.quote: 19 and under and 65 and older; seniors every 18 months absent an eligible condition; adults 20 to 64 by condition or referral
sources.title: What OHIP covers
sources.evidence: OHIP covers routine eye exams for people aged 19 years or younger. If you are 65 years and older and you do not have an eligible medical condition affecting your eyes, OHIP will cover 1 major eye exam once every 18 months and 2 additional follow-up minor assessments. People aged 20 to 64 with certain conditions may be eligible for insured eye exams by an optometrist or doctor.

sources.quote: 18 and under and 65 and older, about one exam a year; 19 to 64 only when medically required
sources.title: Eye Examination Benefits - Province of British Columbia
sources.evidence: Routine eye examinations are an MSP benefit for those 18 years of age and under and 65 years of age and over. Routine eye examinations are not a MSP benefit for individuals aged 19 to 64 years. An eye examination, for patients between the ages of 19 and 64, is an insured benefit only if medically required. Refractive change with no other pathology does not meet the MSP medically required criteria for payment.

sources.quote: 18 and under and 65 and older, one assessment per July to June benefit year
sources.title: Health care services covered in Alberta | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: Children 18 years old and younger, and seniors 65 years and older are eligible for one oculo-visual assessment (complete routine eye exam) and one diagnostic procedure per benefit year (July 1 to June 30) under the AHCIP. Optometrists can charge for insured services that the optometrist deems exceeds the AHCIP benefit and Albertans are responsible for additional costs.

sources.quote: Quebec (RAMQ) | 17 and under and 65 and older
sources.publisher: Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec
sources.title: Optometric services | Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ)
sources.evidence: Children, persons age 65 or over and those with a visual impairment, among others, may benefit from free optometric services. The eye examination is covered by health insurance for children under the age of 18. Persons age 18 to 64 who have been a recipient of a financial assistance program with claim slip for at least the past 12 consecutive months may also benefit from free optometric services.

sources.quote: the regulator since the June 2024 amalgamation
sources.publisher: College of Health and Care Professionals of BC
sources.title: About CHCPBC | CHCPBC
sources.evidence: The CHCPBC was established on June 28, 2024, resulting from the amalgamation of the College of Dietitians of BC, the College of Occupational Therapists of BC, the College of Opticians of BC, the College of Optometrists of BC, the College of Physical Therapists of BC, the College of Psychologists of BC, and the College of Speech and Hearing Health Professionals of BC.

sources.quote: Advertising must be truthful, accurate, verifiable and not misleading.
sources.title: Advertising Guidelines, Including Member and Practice Representation - College of Optometrists of Ontario
sources.evidence: Advertising must not mislead the public, and advertising must not contain a testimonial or comparative or superlative statements. Advertised promotions must be truthful and verifiable and must not be misleading or presented in such a manner as to demean the integrity of the profession.

sources.quote: in Ontario the original prescription is part of the examination fee
sources.title: Optometric Prescriptions: Release of Prescriptions - College of Optometrists of Ontario
sources.evidence: The original prescription is part of the examination fee. Any replacement copies can be charged to the patient at a reasonable fee. A member of the College must provide a patient with a written, signed, and dated prescription for subnormal vision devices, contact lenses or eye glasses, and this prescription must be provided without request from the patient.

sources.quote: healthcare policy blocks remarketing built on health conditions
sources.title: Health in personalized advertising - Advertising Policies Help
sources.evidence: Health content includes physical or mental health conditions, including diseases, sexual health, and chronic health conditions. Google doesn't allow personalized advertising based on personal hardships, which include health conditions, treatments, procedures; advertisers can't use advertiser-curated audiences for health-related sensitive content.
